update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency Indian musical instruments and their legendary exponents (maestros) for Art & Culture Static GK.

string_instruments_chordophones.key_fact: A plucked string instrument widely used in Hindustani classical music. Its invention is traditionally attributed to Amir Khusro.
A fretless string instrument known for its deep, weighty, and introspective sound. It is highly prominent in Hindustani classical music.
An ancient trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer native to Jammu and Kashmir. It typically features 72 to 100 strings.
One of the oldest Indian string instruments, heavily featured in Carnatic music and traditionally associated with Goddess Saraswati.
A bowed string instrument covered with animal skin. It is considered the closest Indian instrument to the human voice.
Though Western in origin, it was heavily adapted into Carnatic classical music in the 18th century and is now a staple.

wind_instruments_aerophones.key_fact: A side-blown flute made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo. Pannalal Ghosh is credited with elevating it to a concert-level instrument.
A double-reed instrument traditionally played at weddings and temples. Ustad Bismillah Khan famously played it at the Red Fort on the eve of India's independence in 1947.

percussion_instruments_membranophones_an.key_fact: Consists of a pair of hand drums (the smaller 'Dayan' and larger 'Bayan'). It is the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
A double-sided drum made of a single piece of wood. It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in a Carnatic music ensemble.
A barrel-shaped, two-headed drum, which is a variant of the Mridangam. It is the standard percussion instrument used in the Dhrupad style of music.
A large, narrow-mouthed earthenware clay pot used as a percussion instrument in Carnatic music.
